entities.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the singular verb וַיַּרְא. The Creator surveys all that he has made, identifying him as the God introduced in Genesis 1:1.

name_review_base.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the singular verb וַיַּרְא. The Creator surveys all that he has made, identifying him as the God introduced in Genesis 1:1.

review.translation: [Then|0] [God|1] [saw|0] [all|3,2] [that|4] [he had made|5], [and behold|6], {it was} [very|8] [good|7]. [Then there was|9] [evening|10], [and there was|11] [morning|12], [the sixth|14] [day|13].

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject. The direct object marker אֶת introduces כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה, “all that he had made.” God surveys his work, and וְהִנֵּה טוֹב מְאֹד gives his assessment, “and behold, it was very good.”
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיַּרְא, “he saw.” The singular verb identifies God as the one who saw כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה, “all that he had made.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural common noun in the absolute state, with singular verbal agreement.

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיַּרְא ‘saw’. אֶת introduces כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה ‘everything he had made’, the direct object of ‘saw’.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה, the relative clause אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה specifies what כָּל includes. God saw “everything he had made,” and וְהִנֵּה טוֹב מְאֹד evaluates it as a whole.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה, “all that he had made,” אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause modifying כָּל. What God had made is what he saw.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה, “all that he had made,” אֱלֹהִים is the understood subject of עָשָׂה. God looks over the whole of his completed work and sees that it is very good.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים describes God looking at all he had made. וְהִנֵּה introduces what he saw about it: טוֹב מְאֹד, “very good.”
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to the presentative interjection הִנֵּה.
analysis.sense: and there was (what one sees or finds)

analysis.evidence: God sees כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה (“all that he had made”). In וְהִנֵּה טוֹב מְאֹד (“and behold, it was very good”), טוֹב expresses his assessment of the whole, and מְאֹד intensifies it.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective used predicatively, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וְהִנֵּה טוֹב מְאֹד, מְאֹד intensifies the preceding adjective טוֹב. God saw that everything he had made was “very good.”
analysis.morphology: Uninflected adverb of degree, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: עֶרֶב is the subject of וַיְהִי. The clause marks the arrival of evening, followed by the parallel וַיְהִי בֹקֶר, “and there was morning,” in the closing formula for the sixth day.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix

analysis.evidence: In וַיְהִי עֶרֶב וַיְהִי בֹקֶר, “there was evening and there was morning,” עֶרֶב is paired with בֹקֶר, “morning,” in the refrain that closes the sixth day.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיְהִי בֹקֶר, the subject בֹקֶר means “morning.” The clause parallels וַיְהִי עֶרֶב and recounts the coming of morning after evening on the sixth day.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ.

analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי בֹקֶר means “and there was morning.” It parallels וַיְהִי עֶרֶב, “and there was evening,” in the closing formula for the sixth day.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: After the sequence of evening and morning, הַשִּׁשִּׁי identifies this day as the sixth in the creation sequence.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun without prefix or suffix. The absolute and construct forms are identical here.

draft.change: Change the Hebrew root key from שדש to שש and make the ordinal’s derivation from שֵׁשׁ explicit. The existing sense “sixth (in order)” already cites Genesis 1:31. Keep the comparative evidence for an older medial d in the etymological discussion.
draft.definition: שִׁשִּׁי is the ordinal adjective formed from שֵׁשׁ, “six.” It identifies the sixth member of a sequence.
draft.evidence: Genesis 1:31 uses the masculine הַשִּׁשִּׁי with יוֹם. Exodus 26:9 shows the derivation within one instruction: six curtains are counted with שֵׁשׁ, and the sixth curtain is singled out with the feminine ordinal הַשִּׁשִּׁית.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 1:31 closes with יוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי, “the sixth day.” The evening-and-morning formula previously closed the fifth day in Genesis 1:23. שִׁשִּׁי gives this day’s position in the sequence, and הַ־ supplies the definite article.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed definite article הַ־ + ordinal adjective שִׁשִּׁי, masculine singular absolute, modifying יוֹם.
